instrument: evidence/census_v10o.c + coalescence counters (rec carries prev/ridx/ring at insert; on a cross-owner class meet the two augmented states are compared). Reproduces the shipped arm exactly (150-trial check: 2 successes, 7611020 records, 6 ring hits).
question: with prev-row + ring state in the transition, must collisions coalesce in the AUGMENTED state (class x prev x ring) for the reduction to succeed?

ratio_row.reading: 0 of 62 class coincidences shared a prev register and 0 shared the 4-entry ring state, i.e. augmented coalescence is at most 4.7 pct of class coincides at 95 pct confidence. That is the expected 2^-11 for prev alone.

solve_equality: x = (a1-a2)/(c2-c1) mod n, then verify [x]P == Q. prev and the ring enter neither the formula nor the check, so a witness never needs augmented agreement.
why_it_matters: The verdict objected that 'failure of point-only coalescence does not imply that matching augmented states cannot coalesce'. Conceded as a logical point and answered empirically: augmented states DO fail to coalesce (0/62), and it does not matter, because the solve is defined on class equality. The success EVENT is class-matching; the WALK STATE is augmented. Those are different objects and the package uses the first for recovery and the second only for stepping.
witness_usable_at_report: 1.000 across all 24 matrix cells (verified == meets exactly, 115..900375 meets per cell) and 62/62 on the instrumented arm. The guarded path does not degrade witness validity; this is not the g1-invert retention failure mode.
